evidence.contextAndScope: chapter28 explains storage geometry, MTD partitions, UBI/UBIFS, U-Boot environment, A/B layout, eMMC boot partitions/RPMB and product storage sizing.
evidence.problemSignalAndCounterevidence: The prior text contained bad-block offsets whose implied erase geometry contradicted one another; unsupported standard sizes, fixed sizing multiples and UBI overhead; unverified fixed-partition/eMMC commands and claims that generic UBI or RPMB automatically supplies atomic OTA/anti-rollback. The existing evaluation explicitly withdrew a device-capacity inference based only on BBT page number.
evidence.causeHypothesisAndAlternatives: Examples from raw NAND, block devices and eMMC hardware partitions were mixed without a pinned device geometry, board ROM format or exact U-Boot configuration. Generic sizing heuristics were stated as standards.
evidence.evidence: Linux MTD docs describe NAND eraseblock handling; Linux UBIFS docs state UBI handles wear-leveling/bad-block abstraction and UBIFS works above UBI volumes. U-Boot v2025.01 mmc docs define `partconf` and its boot/access fields. Those docs do not validate an unspecified device layout or a generic OTA design.
evidence.sampleCoverage: Read full article and published-loop-03 notes, including media table, 1GB fixed-partition map, sizing tables, env offsets, A/B guidance, synthetic BBT transcript, UBI config/overhead, eMMC area size/partconf/genimage examples, workflow and summary. Removed invented geometry/output/commands and fixed-ratio rules. No target device, image, NAND geometry or eMMC EXT_CSD was available.
evidence.decision: Remediated as a device-specific design/verification workflow; distinguished MTD/UBI from block devices; removed synthetic logs, unsupported values and persistent-write recipes. No metadata exception.

U-Boot source docs define legacy script versus FIT script and say legacy images cannot be signed/verified. Standard Boot/bootflow docs define configuration-dependent scan behavior.
